name: Domi
maturity: Working demo plus a live London pilot environment. It has no customers or patients yet, and the compliance paperwork is outstanding.

brand.tone: Plain-spoken, practical and scrupulously honest about what is and isn't built, written for busy home-visit practices in British English.

facts.text: Domi is a diary for home-visit healthcare that refills itself when patients cancel.

source.quote: **Home-visit diaries that refill themselves.**

facts.text: When a patient cancels, Domi works out who on the waiting list could take the slot, then either gives the office a ranked call list, texts the best match and books the first yes, or books them straight in.

source.quote: It either hands the office a ranked call list (many home-visit patients never answer a text), texts the best match and books the first yes, or books them straight in.

facts.text: Domi is built for healthcare that comes to the patient's home, including eye care, hearing, foot care, dental, physio, blood tests, nursing and therapy assessments.

source.quote: The diary for healthcare that comes to the patient's home: eye care, hearing,

facts.text: Domiciliary eye care is the service Domi is built for today, and the demo is an eye-care practice.

source.quote: | **Domiciliary eye care** | Built for it: the demo is an eye-care practice |

facts.text: A cancellation costs a home-visit practice more than a clinic, because the clinician is already on the road and the gap is too short to fill by ringing round.

facts.text: Domi acts on the gap in the way the practice chooses: a ranked call list for the office, an offer by text that books the first yes, or booking the best match straight in.

source.quote: That's a ranked call list for the office, an offer by text that books the first yes, or booking the best match straight in.

facts.text: Patients see the practice's own name in every text, on the booking page and on invoices, never Domi's.

source.quote: **Patients see the practice, not Domi.** Every patient text, the booking page and invoices use the practice's name

facts.text: The refill engine ranks candidates by clinical priority, locality, days waiting and preferred clinician, and shows the reasons for each.

source.quote: Ranking: clinical priority, then local, days waiting, preferred clinician. Each candidate shows the reasons

facts.text: Patients can cancel by texting CANCEL, which starts the refill with no staff involved.

source.quote: A patient texting CANCEL cancels the visit and starts the refill, with no staff involved.

facts.text: New visits are booked where they add the least driving, weighed against how soon the patient needs to be seen.

facts.text: Route planning puts visits that haven't started in the order that drives least, from the clinician's home base and back.

facts.text: A phone-first clinician view shows today's round with drive times, patient records, quick notes and an On my way text to the patient.

source.quote: Phone-first. Today's round with drive times, patient records (alerts, last prescription, glasses, history)

facts.text: The clinician app works offline, syncing notes and visit updates in order when signal returns.

source.quote: notes and visit updates made without signal sync in order when it returns. Signing out wipes the copy

facts.text: A CANCEL reply to a reminder refills that slot a day ahead.

facts.text: With Phone them, the office gets a ranked call list, best match first, with numbers ready, and logs each outcome in one tap.

source.quote: **Phone them** (for practices whose patients don't text; the demo's default is *Text an offer*): the office gets a ranked call list, best match first, with numbers ready, and logs *no answer*, *not interested* or *booked* in one tap.

facts.text: Each NHS sight test visit gets its PCSE notice rule: 48 working hours, 3 weeks for three or more patients at one address, and never more than 8 weeks ahead.

source.quote: Each NHS sight test visit (one address on one day) gets its notice rule: 48 working hours, 3 weeks for three or more at one address, never more than 8 weeks ahead.

facts.text: Bookings that can't meet the PCSE notice are refused unless the ICB's approval is recorded.

source.quote: Bookings that can't meet the notice are refused unless the ICB's approval is recorded.

facts.text: Each visit gets three confirmation calls: when it's booked, in the week before with a 3-hour arrival window from the planned route, and on the working day before.

source.quote: Each visit gets three calls: **CC1** when it's booked (the date only), **CC2** in the week before (a 3-hour arrival window worked out from the planned route), and **CC3** on the working day before (date, time and address).

facts.text: Domi works alongside Opticabase, which stays the record for eye tests and claims: a daily CSV export imports cleanly, matched by Opticabase ID.

facts.text: Domi and Opticabase can't talk to each other yet, so bookings, moves and cancellations made in Domi are copied across to Opticabase by hand from a checklist.

source.quote: The two systems can't talk to each other yet, so that copying is done by hand

facts.text: Pilot results use figures from the diary or from what the office records, never estimates.

source.quote: Every number comes from the diary or from what the office records, never from an estimate

facts.text: Live data sits in a permanent UK database, Supabase Postgres in London, with daily backups and a tested restore.

source.quote: **A permanent UK database:** Supabase Postgres in London (Pro plan, daily backups), with a restore tested by `scripts/restore-test.sh`.
